topics.caution: The explanation turns દાદાજીની 'આખરે તો આ શ્રીકૃષ્ણની ભૂમિ છે… દેહત્યાગ' and the જરા-બાણ-ક્ષમા lines into a theological account, a lesson about forgiveness, or an addition to the story from outside the page.
topics.guidance: Teach it as દાદા's answer to અનેરી's question — what he says the place is and what અનેરી recalls from the 'સિરિયલ' — attributing it to him ('દાદાજી કહે છે કે…'); add no detail of the story beyond the printed lines, and keep any real_life_example inside the child's world (a place their own family visits), not worship instruction.

topics.caution: The explanation explains ગીતામંદિર, the ત્રિવેણીસંગમ snan and the સોમનાથદાદાની સાંજની આરતી as ritual doctrine or compares them with other faiths, or says what a child 'should' do there.
topics.guidance: Describe them as the chapter does — places the family goes and does, with the children's delight at their first river snan; name the three rivers (હિરણ્ય, કપિલા, સરસ્વતી) only as રાજેશભાઈ says them; recall answers and the one-word block for સંગમ stay on the words and the scene, not on belief.

topics.caution: The Gir hosts' dialect (હંધાય, હારું, આંઈ, હાલ્યા), their ચિત્રો, ભરતકામ, દુહાછંદ and ઢોલિયે બેસવું are explained as quaint or 'backward', as errors to correct, or the hosts are labelled with a community name the page does not give them.
topics.guidance: Present the speech as the hosts' own spoken Saurashtra and keep it verbatim, glossing a word at its point of use as દાદા does ('ઢોલિયો એટલે ખાટલો'); describe the art, clothes and singing as અનેરી and the text do, in present tense and with respect, and name the hosts only as printed (શંકરદાન, હીરુબાઈ, વિક્રમભાઈ) without inventing a community for them.

topics.caution: A child could read the lioness-and-cubs scene, or the hosts' calm ('માણસને ન વતાવે', ભેંસો outside and ગાયો inside), as permission to go near wild lions or to copy the cattle arrangement, and the hosts' practice could be generalised into a rule the page does not state.
topics.guidance: Keep the account as the hosts' own words and own cattle-keeping logic, attributed to them ('હીરુબાઈ કહે છે કે…'), and say plainly in the teacher's voice that this is how those who live in the Gir tell it, not something to try; the real_life_example must be something safe in the child's world (a ગાયનો વાડો seen from the road, a zoo or documentary), never approaching an animal, and no recall answer should invite imitation.

topics.caution: મકદુમભાઈ's words 'અમે સીદી છીએ… પૂર્વજો… આફ્રિકાથી' are turned into a lump label, an 'outsider' framing, a history lecture, or details about the સીદી community that the page does not give.
topics.guidance: Use his own name for his community, સીદી, exactly as he says it, and report only what he says — his ancestors came from Africa years ago and 'હવે તો આ ભૂમિ જ અમારું વતન' — attributed to him; teach વતન from his sentence with respect and without surprise, and add no population, origin story or date.

topics.caution: The safari scene (a ભયંકર ત્રાડ, two સાવજ ઘૂરકતા, lions beside the road) is read as thrill-seeking, or the guide's rules are supplemented with safety rules the page does not print.
topics.guidance: Report only the guide's two printed rules (મોટા અવાજે ન બોલવું, પ્લાસ્ટિક ન ફેંકવું) and the printed fact that the vehicles stayed standing until the lions walked out of sight, as the chapter tells it; the explanation may say the children watch from the vehicle with the guide, and any real_life_example stays with a school trip's guide-and-rules, never closeness to an animal.

chapter_level.guidance: The Gir and Saurashtra practices (living beside lions, the hosts' hospitality, the Sasan safari) are told by the chapter through its characters' voices; attribute each claim to the speaker, keep the text's own claim that people and lions live 'એકમેકને નડ્યા વગર' as the guide's statement, and supply no outside fact about the Gir lions, their numbers or conservation.

સોમનાથ, ભાલકાતીર્થ, ગીતામંદિર, ત્રિવેણીસંગમ and the આરતી are living devotion inside travel prose; teach the travel-writing and the words, never theology or comparative religion, and keep the real printed photograph of the temple as page matter with no authored likeness.
